input:
This executive summary reviews delivery performance at a contract packaging firm which runs 4 plants and has revenue of $83 million per year, and it considers a proposal to invest in a new scheduling system. The evidence base for the review consists of order records for 12 months, covering 14394 orders in total.

Over the last two quarters, on-time delivery was 88%, which falls short of the target of 95% that the business has set itself. Overtime cost was $2.6 million last year, up 18% on the year before, and the order backlog currently stands at 3.8 weeks, compared with 1.7 weeks a year ago, so the position has deteriorated on several measures at the same time.

A particularly striking feature of the data is the extent to which the problem is concentrated: Plant 2 accounts for 64% of late orders, which suggests that the difficulties are not spread evenly across the business. A scheduling system for all plants is quoted at $328k, while Plant 2 alone is $119k. An internal estimate, which it should be stressed is not a vendor figure, puts the overtime reduction at Plant 2 at 15-20% in the first year. The recommendation under consideration is therefore to install at Plant 2 first and to hold the other plants until Plant 2 results are reported, with the operations director owning the scheduling programme.
